source.title: From complex to simple : hierarchical free-energy landscape renormalized in deep neural networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or garbling affecting the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: Uses replica theory and Monte Carlo dynamics to study solutions of deep perceptrons under random input/output constraints, a different method from training-error tests. It does not test whether standard SGD reaches those solutions.
record.gate_note: The paper studies random input/output constraints and their solution landscape. Its Monte Carlo simulations measure overlap and energy relaxation, not training error or test error. Results cited from other work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes equilibrium solution-space geometry and Metropolis relaxation in sign-activation perceptrons. It does not establish that stochastic gradient training fits random labels, compare fitting times for true and random labels, or measure any other claim version. Replica overlaps and soft constraint energy are not training-error measurements.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors predict spatially heterogeneous glass–liquid–glass and crystal–liquid–crystal structures for random constraints and teacher–student settings, respectively. Random-constraint simulations qualitatively support heterogeneous relaxation. Proposed explanations of learning efficiency and generalization remain speculative, with finite-width effects, the tree approximation, and the practical symmetry-breaking mechanism acknowledged as limitations.
record.recipe_differences: Replica analysis of solution-space structure, with low-temperature Metropolis simulations of relaxational dynamics; not SGD training-error measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported landscape and relaxation vary with constraint strength α, layer, network depth, and width.

fits_no_version.finding: Under random binary input/output constraints, the replica calculation predicts successive glass transitions from the boundaries inward, with αg(l) approximately 2.7(3) exp(1.03(2)l) and penetration depth proportional to ln α.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The studied perceptron's equilibrium solution space develops spatially heterogeneous glassy structure as constraint density increases.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 3.3.4 infers exponentially growing typical storage capacity with depth from the glass-transition scaling. This concerns existence of compatible solutions within the theoretical approximation, rather than their attainment by training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Typical random-constraint storage capacity grows exponentially with depth in the studied theoretical model.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4, Figures 16–18, reports slower Metropolis relaxation near boundaries and at larger α, faster overlap relaxation in deeper systems, and finite-width truncation of slow dynamics. Energy relaxation does not establish zero classification error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low-temperature Metropolis relaxation in the random-constraint perceptron varies with layer, constraint density, depth, and width.

record.problems: The theory uses a tree approximation that neglects inter-layer loops and fluctuations. The authors note that its infinite-width phase transitions become crossovers at finite width. Simulations use low-temperature Metropolis dynamics rather than realistic learning algorithms and do not measure training or test error.
record.rows_left_out: No results directly measure training error or test error, so no result qualifies as a row for the claim versions. The paper's theoretical order parameters and simulation relaxation measures do not establish whether training fits random labels.

untested.parts: Whether standard networks trained with stochastic gradient methods achieve near-zero random-label training error with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and chance test performance.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and convergence as the corrupted-label fraction increases. Increasing α changes the number of constraints, not the corruption fraction.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs to zero training error.
Perfect training fit and steady test-error degradation across increasing fractions of corrupted labels.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Temporal ordering of learning shared real-data patterns and memorizing noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's classification of V1 as tested_not_extracted: no stated version is tested. The empty result-row list is appropriate. Perfect boundary agreement defines the theoretical solution ensemble; it is not an observed training outcome.

versions.untested_parts: Whether SGD reaches zero training error; unchanged architecture and hyperparameters relative to true-label training; test error at chance; comparison with generalization on true labels.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
